To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the combination of a hierarchical, rule-based gesture classification scheme with an active vocabulary yields a robust and efficient gesture recognition system; b) the system can be used in an automotive environment to control various infotainment systems and c) the system is able to adapt its active gesture vocabulary to the current operating environment.

1) the combination of hand gestures and head gestures yields a very intuitive and robust interaction style for controlling in-vehicle infotainment systems, 2) a combination of preprocessing techniques and a hierarchical classification scheme is an appropriate approach to achieve robust gesture recognition, 3) a context-sensitive reduction of the active gesture vocabulary is an important feature for robust gesture recognition, and 4) the proposed system can be easily adapted to other gesture-based applications like sign language recognition.

a robust multimodal gesture recognition system for controlling automotive infotainment systems can be realized using a combination of rule-based classification and a context-dependent gesture vocabulary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and evaluation of a multimodal gesture recognition system for automotive infotainment applications.
the development of an efficient and flexible gesture interface for controlling infotainment applications in automotive environments.
the development of a gesture-based user-interface which is robust and reliable, yet intuitive and easy to use.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of hand gestures with head gestures is a very promising interaction style for controlling automotive infotainment systems, and that the proposed system is a viable solution for this application.

the proposed system can be easily integrated into existing automotive architectures and that the performance can be improved significantly by adapting the active gesture vocabulary to the context of use.

a video-based gesture recognition system for automotive infotainment applications can be realized in a cost-efficient way using a combination of standard hardware and a hierarchical, rule-based classification scheme.
